description: Task 2.3 - C/C++ runtime hook via GCC -finstrument-functions. The C FFI (xplainit-c/src/lib.rs) currently exposes create/free/enable/disable/get_events/clear/statistics but has NO recording entry points. Add C FFI functions that record function enter/exit/exception events, provide the __cyg_profile_func_enter/exit glue that user code links against, and prove a real instrumented C program produces captured events. Toolchains gcc 11.5 and clang 15 are PRESENT, so this is fully buildable and verifiable in-sandbox. Depends on FEAT-001. Files: xplainit-c/src/lib.rs, xplainit-c/include/xplainit-c.h (regenerated by cbindgen), xplainit-c/build.rs, new xplainit-c/src or a small C shim, xplainit-c/examples/example_traced.c, xplainit-c/examples/build.sh.
steps: Add recording FFI to xplainit-c/src/lib.rs as #[no_mangle] extern "C" functions on the existing XplainitHandle: xplainit_on_function_enter(handle, const char* name, const char* file, uint32_t line), xplainit_on_function_exit(handle, const char* name, const char* file, uint32_t line), and xplainit_on_exception(handle, const char* type, const char* message, const char* file, uint32_t line). Each builds the corresponding xplainit_core::ExecutionEvent (FunctionEnter/FunctionExit/Exception) and calls event_store().record(...). Follow the null-check + Mutex-lock pattern used by the existing FFI. Make xplainit_enable/xplainit_disable/xplainit_is_enabled track a real enabled flag (currently they are no-ops) so recording can be gated; store the flag in XplainitHandle.

Provide the -finstrument-functions bridge. Because __cyg_profile_func_enter/exit receive function POINTERS (not names), add either (a) a small C shim (xplainit-c/instrument.c or similar) implementing __cyg_profile_func_enter/__cyg_profile_func_exit with __attribute__((no_instrument_function)) that resolves the function address to a name via dladdr() and forwards to the FFI recording functions using a global/thread handle set by an init call; or (b) document dladdr resolution inside that shim. Provide an init function (e.g. xplainit_instrument_init) that creates/sets the global handle the shim uses. Ensure the shim itself and the FFI are compiled with no_instrument_function to avoid infinite recursion.

If cbindgen (xplainit-c/build.rs) regenerates xplainit-c/include/xplainit-c.h on build, let it regenerate and commit the updated header with the new prototypes. Verify the header contains the new functions.

Add/expand xplainit-c/examples/example_traced.c: a C program with a simple function, a recursive function (e.g. factorial), and a function that triggers an error path, compiled with `-finstrument-functions` and linked against libxplainit_c plus the shim and -ldl. After running, it should fetch xplainit_get_events / statistics and print them.

Update xplainit-c/examples/build.sh to build libxplainit_c via `cargo build --release`, compile the shim + example with gcc `-finstrument-functions ... -L../../target/release -lxplainit_c -ldl`, run the resulting binary, and assert (grep/exit code) that captured events are non-empty and include the expected function names. Make the script exit non-zero on failure so it is a real gate.
Run examples/build.sh end to end and confirm real events are captured from the instrumented C program.

Add a Rust unit test in xplainit-c/src/lib.rs that calls the new xplainit_on_function_enter/exit through the FFI (unsafe) against a created handle and asserts get_events reflects the recorded events and get_statistics counts them; and a disabled-handle test asserting nothing is recorded when disabled.
acceptance_criteria: xplainit-c/src/lib.rs exposes xplainit_on_function_enter/exit/exception that actually record events, and enable/disable/is_enabled track a real flag that gates recording.
xplainit-c/include/xplainit-c.h contains the new prototypes (regenerated by cbindgen).
examples/build.sh compiles an -finstrument-functions program, runs it, and asserts non-empty captured events including expected function names; it exits non-zero on failure.
New Rust FFI unit tests pass proving events are recorded when enabled and not recorded when disabled.
cargo build --release, cargo test, and cargo clippy -D warnings all pass; Python suites remain green.
findings:
Implemented C/C++ runtime hook via -finstrument-functions and real recording FFI. Details:
- xplainit-c/src/lib.rs: added #[no_mangle] extern "C" xplainit_on_function_enter/exit/exception building ExecutionEvent::FunctionEnter/FunctionExit/Exception and calling runtime.event_store().record(...). Added an AtomicBool `enabled` flag to XplainitHandle (default true on create); xplainit_enable/disable/is_enabled now set/read it, and all three recording functions return 0 and record nothing when disabled or on null handle. Added helper cstr_to_string for null-safe CStr->String.
- Added chrono and uuid deps to xplainit-c/Cargo.toml (Cargo.lock unchanged - versions already resolved by sibling crates).
- New shim xplainit-c/lib/trace.c + trace.h: implements __cyg_profile_func_enter/exit (all functions marked __attribute__((no_instrument_function)) to avoid self-recursion), resolves func addresses to names via dladdr() (-ldl), and exposes xplainit_instrument_init/get_events/get_statistics/report_exception/shutdown around a global XplainitHandle.
- cbindgen (build.rs) regenerated xplainit-c/include/xplainit-c.h; it now contains the three new prototypes (verified).
- Rewrote xplainit-c/examples/example_traced.c (simple add/multiply, recursive factorial, safe_divide error path reporting a DivisionByZero exception) and build.sh into a real gate: cargo build --release -p xplainit-c, compile shim+example with -finstrument-functions -rdynamic -I../include -I../lib -L target/release -lxplainit_c -ldl, run with LD_LIBRARY_PATH, and assert (grep + exit code) non-empty events including add/multiply/factorial/calculate_something and a DivisionByZero exception. Runs green end to end (16 events in the stats batch; JSON batch shows recursion + exception).
- IMPORTANT gotcha: RuntimeEngine.get_events() AND get_statistics() DRAIN the event store (get_events -> event_store.drain()). The example therefore dumps the events JSON first, then re-runs a subset before reading statistics. Rust unit tests account for this too.
- .gitignore had broad `lib/`, `*.so`, `*.out` rules (Python egg artifacts) that ignored the shim source; added negation `!xplainit-c/lib/**` and an explicit ignore for the built `xplainit-c/examples/example_traced` binary.
- Added 6 new Rust FFI unit tests (enabled records enter/exit reflected in get_statistics and get_events JSON; exception recording; disabled handle records nothing; null-handle safety). cargo test -p xplainit-c = 11 passed.
Verification all green: cargo build --release clean; cargo test (whole workspace) all pass; cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -D warnings clean; xplainit-c/examples/build.sh PASSED; Python suites still 3/3, 11/11, decorators pass. gcc 11.5 used; dladdr resolves symbols correctly (needs -rdynamic, which build.sh supplies).
